full_judgment: 10. In the case of Md Nizamuddin vs State, 30 DLR 49 where it was held that when a vested right has been accrued to an accused it cannot be taken away by subsequent amendment of the law. In that case, appellant Md Nizamuddin challenged the law of presenting the appeal to the Appellant Tribunal under section 30 of the Special Tribunal Act, 1974 as before insertion of section 30 of the Act appellant's right to presenting the appeal before the High Court Division was accrued and a vested right arising from the pending proceeding, In the case of Md Irtiza vs State, PLD 1959 (WP) Karachi, 94, the question raised is that after the commitment of the petitioners to Court of Sessions, case was initiated on 9-5-1954, by the learned Magistrate on 30-4- 1956 under section 167(G) of the Sea Customs Act, an amendment of section 3 of the Act was made on 2-8-1957 rendering the offences under section 167(G) of the Act triable by the Customs Authority. It was held that since the legal proceeding was instituted on 9-5-1954, will continue under the repealed provisions. In the case of Arshad Ali Sk vs Bangladesh, 29 DLR 301, where question arose whether after the repeal of the Bengal Tenancy Act and coming into force of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, an application for setting aside sale under section 173(4) of BT Act will lie. The application was filed on 2-11-66 for setting aside a sale held on 19-3-1952 in rent execution case No. 1308 of 1951. It was held that the application is maintainable In the case of Akhtar Hossain Khan vs State, 29 DLR (SC) 101 where the question mooted was that PO 50 of 1972 having been repealed on 9- 2-74 any police investigation in process before 9-2-74 in view of the decision in Mridha s case [26 DLR (SC) 17] could not be continued under PO 50, inasmuch as the saving clause under section 36(2)(b) of Special Powers Act has, provided fox the continuance of the cases that were pending under the said Act, and view of the aforementioned Mridhas decision the time at which cognisance of an offence under PO 50 commences is the date on which the charge sheet is submitted under Article 4of that Act and in the present case the Charge sheet was submitted when PO 50 was dead. It was held on reference to the case of Sona vs State, 22 DLR (SC) 155 that repeal of the Act shall not affect pending proceedings under it. Moreover, proceedings may be continued and punishment may be imposed as if repealing Act has not been passed.
